prompt:
Write one compact, entirely fictional Ohio trial-court memorandum and one fictional record exhibit.

This is a matched-pair unit-test fixture, not client work. The memorandum must expressly invoke HUD Handbook 4350.3 REV-1 ¶ 8-13.B and ask the court to rule on that doctrine. Apply only this supplied contract:
- identify project-based assistance and applicable HUD lease/handbook provision
- quote the notice's ten-day discussion advisement
- show tenant timely requested discussion and owner did not honor it (make request applicable)

Target requirement for an exact-deletion mutation: show tenant timely requested discussion and owner did not honor it (make request applicable).
Required procedural posture and facts: Write for a project-based assisted tenant opposing the owner's termination and eviction because the tenant requested the offered discussion within ten days and the owner filed without holding it.

Hard requirements:
1. Return one JSON object with exactly these string keys: title, brief_template, target_paragraph, record_text.
2. brief_template must contain the literal marker [[TARGET_ELEMENT_PARAGRAPH]] exactly once, on its own line between blank lines.
3. target_paragraph must be one short standalone argument paragraph that clearly applies ONLY the target element. It must not introduce a fact needed by another element.
4. Every nonconditional nontarget element must be expressly and separately applied in the argument. The target element must not be applied anywhere except target_paragraph. Mere facts in the statement-of-facts section do not count as application.
5. record_text must directly support every fact used for every element, including the target. The record will be identical in both arms.
6. Include concrete dates, amounts, notices, and actions sufficient to make the analysis unambiguous.
7. Keep brief_template between 1,400 and 2,800 characters and record_text between 500 and 1,500 characters.
8. Do not mention this experiment, the marker, a mutation, omitted text, a control, or a mutant in the filing or record.
9. Use no authority except HUD Handbook 4350.3 REV-1 ¶ 8-13.B and authorities literally embedded in the supplied element descriptions.
10. Invent names and facts distinct from common examples; do not use Maple Apartments, Jordan Lee, Oak Street Homes, Morgan Taylor, Lakeview Rentals, Alex Rivera, or Mei Chen.
11. Use a caption/title, Statement of Facts, Argument, and Conclusion. The party's requested ruling must match the required procedural posture.
12. Do not use the words "element," "requirement," "satisfy," or any internal identifier in the filing. Write natural legal argument. Do not repeat, paraphrase, summarize, or draw the conclusion of target_paragraph after the marker. Outside target_paragraph, avoid these target-only phrases: failed to honor, did not honor, without holding, never held, owner ignored, required to honor, failure to comply.
13. Do not characterize which court issued a cited decision and do not add a quotation or holding beyond the supplied rule contract.

The mutant will be derived mechanically by removing target_paragraph. Do not write two briefs.

Shenequa Bryant resides at Cedarbrook Housing, a project-based Section 8 assisted property. On February 10, 2023, Cedarbrook Housing served Bryant with a notice of termination stating that she had 10 days to request a discussion. The notice quoted HUD Handbook 4350.3 REV-1 ¶ 8-13.B and stated: 'You have the right to discuss this termination with management within 10 days of receiving this notice.' On February 14, 2023, Bryant timely requested a discussion by email. Cedarbrook Housing did not respond or hold a discussion. On February 24, 2023, Cedarbrook Housing filed this eviction action.

Argument
Cedarbrook Housing's termination notice complied with HUD Handbook 4350.3 REV-1 ¶ 8-13.B by quoting the advisement. The project-based assistance is governed by this handbook provision.

[[TARGET_ELEMENT_PARAGRAPH]]

The handbook requires that the owner honor a timely request for discussion. Bryant's request was made within the 10-day period.

Conclusion
The court should rule in favor of Shenequa Bryant because Cedarbrook Housing did not comply with HUD Handbook 4350.3 REV-1 ¶ 8-13.B.
